exposure: History of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy
cohort: A total of 173 cases (postpartum women at risk of postpartum depression) were studied and compared with 173 controls (postpartum women without risk of postpartum depression) at a Peruvian hospital.
finding: The prevalence of postpartum depression was 18.8%, and it was significantly associated with age under 20 years, higher education level, single marital status, poor relationship with partner, use of psychotropic drugs, complications during labor, cesarean delivery, history of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy, and employment status.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of postpartum depression (OR: 3.3).
cross-section timing: 15 to 30 days after delivery, between May and October 2022
